_comment: Writes the three timelines of the full product demo (under 5 minutes, no slides), Video.mp4 in Group19.zip: Part C. Generated by demo/make_timeline_demo.py; record with REPLAY_STEP_PACE=0.35.

steps.evaluate: await fetch('/__replay/clock?t=10:30'); const r = await fetch('/api/email/clock', {cache: 'no-store'}); window.threadpilotClock = await r.json(); window.threadpilotClockAnchor = performance.now();

steps.say: 10:30 · Back at the desk. “Was yesterday’s assembly output normal?”
A judgement tool with a written definition: 455 pieces against 687–807 for the previous eight Tuesdays, 39% below.

type.text: How is the TrendCart order doing?

steps.say: A vague question: TrendCart has six active orders, so it asks instead of guessing.
Only one is a scarf: ORD-005. “Show more” lists the planner’s reading, each tool call and the rows behind the answer.

steps.evaluate: await fetch('/__replay/clock?t=11:15'); const r = await fetch('/api/email/clock', {cache: 'no-store'}); window.threadpilotClock = await r.json(); window.threadpilotClockAnchor = performance.now();

steps.say: 11:15 · A customer wants 800 hoodies by the 25th.

type.text: Can we take 800 hoodies by the 25th?

steps.say: It asks the one thing that changes the answer: ready at the factory, or delivered?
An estimate, not a yes: unlikely. The queue finishes 30 April; it names the bottleneck and the outside workshops.
The Feasibility page runs the same tool over the whole queue and shows why.
The same figures as the chat: 30 April, five days late, because the later stages are over capacity before the 25th.

steps.evaluate: await fetch('/__replay/clock?t=14:30'); const r = await fetch('/api/email/clock', {cache: 'no-store'}); window.threadpilotClock = await r.json(); window.threadpilotClockAnchor = performance.now();

steps.say: 14:30 · The core task: chase a stalled order, typed the way it is said on the floor.

type.text: ORD 5 hasn’t moved in a week, chase knitting

steps.say: It checks the claim against the record first (last activity 24 March, 8 days: true), then drafts to knitting.
Preview first. Nothing is sent until the manager confirms this exact draft.
Confirmed and sent. On the live system it leaves from the manager’s own mailbox.

type.text: Remind me tmrw 10am if knitting doesn’t reply

steps.say: A standing watch: at 10:00 tomorrow the server checks, and notifies only if no reply was recorded.
Every action is logged, with recipient, orders and subject.
It also speaks first, but rationed: an alert only for a decision needed today, at most 3 a day.
Honesty under pressure. A question the data cannot answer:

type.text: What revenue did the TrendCart orders bring in this quarter?

steps.say: No prices in the records, so no revenue figure. It says what it can answer instead.

type.text: Chase ord 29, stuck at washing since last wk

steps.say: A wrong premise: the record says ORD-029 moved today. It says so, and asks before writing anything.
Not in the records, and it says so. It never invents an order, a stage or a number.
Every number comes from a tool with its rows · it asks instead of guessing · by voice or by hand, nothing leaves without a confirmed preview.
